tools.name: refund_and_notify_customer
tools.description: Issues a refund to the customer's original payment for an order through Stripe and emails the customer a refund confirmation.

params.name: payment_intent_id
params.description: Stripe PaymentIntent ID of the order payment

tools.code:
import smtplib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from email.message import EmailMessage

import stripe


@dataclass
class RefundResult:
    refund_id: str
    status: str
    notified: bool


def refund_and_notify_customer(payment_intent_id: str, amount_cents: int, customer_email: str) -> RefundResult:
    refund = stripe.Refund.create(payment_intent=payment_intent_id, amount=amount_cents)
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["Subject"] = "Your refund has been issued"
    msg["From"] = "orders@shop.example.com"
    msg["To"] = customer_email
    msg.set_content(f"We refunded {amount_cents / 100:.2f} to your original payment method.")
    with smtplib.SMTP("localhost") as server:
        server.send_message(msg)
    return RefundResult(refund.id, refund.status, True)

tools.name: get_order_details
tools.description: Looks up an order by ID and returns its status, customer, line items, and totals. Does not change anything.
tools.code:
import sqlite3
from contextlib import closing
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
from typing import Optional

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("orders")

DB_PATH = "/var/data/store.db"


@dataclass
class LineItem:
    sku: str
    name: str
    quantity: int
    unit_price_cents: int


@dataclass
class OrderDetails:
    found: bool
    order_id: str
    status: Optional[str] = None
    customer_id: Optional[str] = None
    customer_email: Optional[str] = None
    placed_at: Optional[str] = None
    subtotal_cents: int = 0
    shipping_cents: int = 0
    tax_cents: int = 0
    total_cents: int = 0
    items: list = field(default_factory=list)


def _fetch_items(conn, order_id):
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT sku, name, quantity, unit_price_cents FROM order_items WHERE order_id = ?",
        (order_id,),
    ).fetchall()
    return [LineItem(*r) for r in rows]


@mcp.tool()
def get_order_details(order_id: str, include_items: bool = True) -> dict:
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)) as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT o.status, o.customer_id, c.email, o.placed_at, "
            "o.subtotal_cents, o.shipping_cents, o.tax_cents "
            "FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id "
            "WHERE o.id = ?",
            (order_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return asdict(OrderDetails(found=False, order_id=order_id))
        items = _fetch_items(conn, order_id) if include_items else []
    status, customer_id, email, placed_at, subtotal, shipping, tax = row
    details = OrderDetails(
        found=True,
        order_id=order_id,
        status=status,
        customer_id=customer_id,
        customer_email=email,
        placed_at=placed_at,
        subtotal_cents=subtotal,
        shipping_cents=shipping,
        tax_cents=tax,
        total_cents=subtotal + shipping + tax,
        items=items,
    )
    return asdict(details)
